To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhalation of crocidolite asbestos fibres in guinea pigs and rats results in the formation of fibrous plaques in the alveolar interstitium, and that these fibrous plaques are composed of collagen, fibronectin, and elastin, as well as of a variety of inflammatory cells.
inhaled crocidoline fibers cause lung fibrosis in rats and guinea pigs.
the NWC crocidolite was more fibrogenic than the TVL crocidolite, and that the fibrogenic potency of the NWC fibres increased with their aspect ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of compounds for the treatment of cancer.
the effects of asbestos exposure on lung function and respiratory health in workers.
the effects of asbestos inhalation on the lungs of animals, with particular reference to the role of fibrogenesis and the development of lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the inhalation of crocidolite by rats and guinea pigs for a period of 400 hours, at a concentration of 0.5 mg/m3, does not produce any significant changes in the lungs, except that in some animals there is evidence of the presence of a few fibres in the alveolar region of the lung.

the inhalation of crocidolite dusts, in the concentrations employed, produced in guinea-pigs, in addition to a generalised fibrosis, the formation of nodules and of pleural plaques, and in rats, a generalised fibrotic condition.
the inhalation of NWC crocidolite by rats and guinea- pigs produces an increase in the incidence of lung tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of the inhaled fibres were similar to those produced by intratracheal injections of the same fibres.
the NWC crocidolite is less toxic than the TVL crocidolite and that the NWC fibres are more readily cleared than the TVL fibres from the lungs of rats.
the inhaled fibres of NWC and TVL crocidolites are equally potent as carcinogens in the lungs of rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of crocidolites are different from the effects of chrysotile asbestos.
the risk of developing mesothelioma after exposure to asbestos is very small.
the effects of inhaled fibrous dusts are not necessarily confined to those fibres which are retained in the lungs.
